corrections_after_review_and_observation: The render path now applies neck compensation to CPU actors as well as the human; human camera head aiming still runs afterwards.

All native head contacts including interference headers select Header and suppress residual torso movement. Non-foot/head contacts and special/retained states preserve the authored chain, including keeper throws and catches.
Ball and target context use the inverse current native body orientation, including authored turns and heading adjustment, instead of counting an already-completed turn again from startAngle.

The initial quick run passed all contact, pose, rendered-application, first-person and toggle checks, but its easy/hard pass comparison mixed a final rendered delta with native contact preparation and arm projection. Different native clips have different baseline deltas. That comparison now measures the actual isolated situational before/after FK response; separate per-scenario checks still require final rendered application, unchanged root/feet and bounded anatomy. No contact or anatomical tolerances were relaxed.

The first full-match fixture assumed chasing an autonomous opponent would guarantee a collision and sent M before F2 in one key chord. The CPU evaded the chase and M could be consumed before setup. The corrected fixture positions the real AI opponent first, then sends M separately and requires an actual in-range contest, protective requests on both actors, and the CPU native full-body protective clip. Gameplay, collision radii and impulse/arm/contact tolerances were not changed to pass the fixture.

limitations: Rendered tests use native Linux/X11 and an SDL virtual Xbox controller. Windows was cross-compiled for x64 and its actual package validated; no Windows GUI or physical Xbox session was available.
334 profiles and 1254 metadata-compatible candidate pairs are procedural descriptors over existing sources, not independent captures or exhaustively rendered contexts.
The new action layer adds bounded torso/arm preparation and recovery. Existing feet, action selection and weighted-skin contact acceptance remain authoritative.
Final rendered additive magnitudes also include native contact preparation and anatomical projection. Their magnitudes cannot isolate or rank the new layer across different authored sources.
Balance remains reduced and animation-guided with bounded joint motors during falls, not a trained whole-body muscular policy.
Each actor has a local Bullet floor; player interaction still combines native collisions, reciprocal impulses and bounded shirt traction. Collision proxies and cloth are approximations.
